newsitem.title: FRANCE: French high court rules stricter norms for layoffs.
newsitem.headline: French high court rules stricter norms for layoffs.

text.p: The French high court, the cour de cassation, on Thursday upheld an appeals court ruling requiring stricter guarantees from companies proposing layoff programmes.

The appeals court handed down its ruling in May 1995, scrapping a 1993 plan by the Paris department store Samaritaine entailing 121 layoffs. It said the plan was too vague in its descriptions of job reclassifications and which workers would be affected.

"The social plan that the employer is required to present to staff representatives should include a reclassification plan with concrete and precise measures to avoid layoffs or limit the number," the high court said.
A source at the French employers' federation CNPF told Reuters the organisation was "very concerned by this judicial shift."
